Certain vintage and rare children's books can command thousands of dollars depending on their edition, printing history, and condition.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b8qWmA6xrR0)

### Top Valuable Children's Books & Estimated Values

- **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** by J.K. Rowling (1997 UK first edition): Up to **$85,620** (only 500 copies were printed in the first run, many sent to libraries).[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)[[2]](https://www.redfoxrarebooks.com/blog/2025/4/7/here-are-the-top-10-of-childrens-collectible-first-editions)
- **The Hobbit** by J.R.R. Tolkien (1937 UK first edition): Around **$65,000**.[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)
- **Where the Wild Things Are** by Maurice Sendak (1963 first edition/signed): **$5,200 to $25,000**.[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)
- **Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland** by Lewis Carroll (1865 first edition or signed Dali edition): **$20,000+**.[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)[[2]](https://www.redfoxrarebooks.com/blog/2025/4/7/here-are-the-top-10-of-childrens-collectible-first-editions)
- **Winnie-the-Pooh / The House at Pooh Corner** by A.A. Milne (1926–1928 first editions): **$4,500 to $17,580** (especially with original dust jackets or signatures).[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:1591112196373376395&ibp=oshop)
- **The Wonderful Wizard of Oz** by L. Frank Baum (1900 first edition): Around **$8,800**.[[1]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)
- **Stuart Little** by E.B. White (1945 first edition): Around **$495** (higher if paired with the rare $2.00 first-state dust jacket).[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:13968058486484644607&ibp=oshop)
- **Little Golden Books** (e.g., *The Poky Little Puppy* ): Common copies sell for $1 to $5, but mint-condition first editions (identified by the letter "A" on the last page) can fetch **$100 to $700** , particularly if they retain original promotional items.[[1]](https://www.facebook.com/66UniqueAntiques/videos/the-value-of-little-golden-books-and-how-to-identify-1st-editions-childrensbooks/929720212855802/)



---

### What Makes a Children's Book Valuable?

- **First Edition / First Printing:** Being the very first run off the press is the primary driver of value.
- **Dust Jackets:** An original, unclipped dust jacket can multiply a book's value exponentially.
- **Condition:** Copies without heavy wear, scribbles, tears, or missing pages are worth vastly more.
- **Signatures or Inscriptions:** Books signed or inscribed by the author or illustrator command premium collector prices.[[1]](https://www.sixbookshop.com/blog/6-rare-childrens-books-worth-money)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b8qWmA6xrR0)[[3]](https://www.facebook.com/66UniqueAntiques/videos/the-value-of-little-golden-books-and-how-to-identify-1st-editions-childrensbooks/929720212855802/)[[4]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)[[5]](https://booksofwonder.com/collections/old-rare-1)

references.title: Stuart Little, E. B. White-1945 1st Edition, Harpers 1st State $2.00 Dust Jacket
references.text: E. B. White, Stuart Little. Harper & Brothers, New York & London, 1945. First Edition, First Printing, in the scarce Harper first‐state dust jacket priced at $2.00. White’s first book for children, illustrated throughout with Garth Williams’s iconic pen‐and‐ink drawings. 8vo. 131pp - A very good copy in a very good or better unclipped jacket. Harper’s original tan pictorial cloth stamped in green and white, with green pictorial endpapers; Corners and spine tips lightly bumped and rubbed, a small mark to the lower front cover, ex‐libris label to the half‐title, and a neat New Mexico bookstore label to the rear pastedown. The jacket is bright and attractive, with light wear to folds and spine tips, gentle sunning to the spine, and mild toning to the rear panel. A charming and presentable first printing of White’s beloved classic, increasingly hard to find in collectible condition with the original $2.00 jacket.
